notes.text: CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

notes.text: Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

cwe.name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components

notes.text:
The repository is SSA's 2018 fork of GitHub Inc.'s `github/government.github.com` marketing site, created solely to contribute a data-list entry upstream. SSA's total contribution — six commits, all from `open.source@ssa.gov` on 2018-07-27, verified against the git history at the reviewed commit:

```diff
# 32a9f1e / ae54031 — _data/governments.yml ("U.S. Federal" section)
+  - SSAgov
# f0885ce / a295d10 — _data/governments.yml (dead-link removal)
-  - OntarioDigital
# d00a9a9 — _data/civic_hackers.yml (dead-link removal)
-  - spendb
# b2af669 — _data/research.yml (dead-link removal)
-  - scalability-llnl
```

The reviewed commit `0580274` is a merge authored from a `github.com` maintainer address on 2018-07-31, combining SSA's contribution branch (`patch-1`) with the then-current upstream branch; the last push was 2018-08-01 and the repository has been dormant since. No SSA-authored code, configuration, workflow, hostname, or secret exists anywhere in it. Of the eight branches, `patch-1` is SSA's contribution branch (YAML edits only) and the other six non-default branches are upstream feature branches inherited at fork time, authored 2015–2018 from non-SSA addresses.

Because the repository is a 2018 snapshot of a third-party (GitHub Inc.) codebase whose only surviving SSA-authored content is one YAML list line (`_data/governments.yml:701`, confirmed by blame), static-analysis, dependency, and secret-scan results it produces are upstream-attributable — see *Not filed* for the full disposition of all 33 scanner results. None represents an SSA vulnerability. The repository also is not deployed: `CNAME` names `government.github.com`, a GitHub-owned domain already bound to the upstream repository's own Pages deployment, and GitHub Pages will not bind the same custom domain to a second repository.

Filed as Informational because dormant contribution forks under an agency GitHub organization create recurring false-positive load on organization-wide security scanning and expose the agency to supply-chain-alert fatigue for code it neither wrote nor operates.

Additional affected files (entire file): N/A — Informational
